hubs.name: hub_job_candidate

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details
satellites.description: Business entity register last-changed timestamp; rowguid excluded as technical metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name
satellites.description: Person type and name details with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Ordinary name/type reporting data; carries the Person last-modified timestamp.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_consent
satellites.description: Email promotion consent with full history.
satellites.split_rationale: Compliance-sensitive consent split out for audit history and access control.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive
satellites.description: Sensitive XML additional contact info and demographics.
satellites.split_rationale: Sensitive classification and XML data type; restricted separately.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: All email addresses of a person, numbered within the person, with history.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone
satellites.description: All telephone numbers of a person qualified by phone number type, with history.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt excluded.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source; credential values never loaded.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street address details with history.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of an address.
satellites.split_rationale: Personal geographic data and spatial data type.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type source identifier and last change.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type source identifier and last change.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name with history of renames.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name with visible renames.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State or province code, no-genuine-code flag and identifier.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of a state or province, tracked over time; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Territory assignment changes independently and needs its own history.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_contact_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the contact relationship.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_details
satellites.description: Employee job and employment-status attributes: job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active/inactive flag, network login, and the last-modified timestamp.
satellites.split_rationale: Employment attributes that are not sensitive and change slowly. ModifiedDate is kept only here. rowguid is left out because it has no business meaning (REQ-006).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_sensitive
satellites.description: Restricted personal data about employees: national ID number, date of birth, gender and marital status.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by data classification (PII), so access can be restricted to authorised HR users.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Leave balances (vacation and sick-leave hours remaining). The satellite builds a history of balance readings over time.
satellites.split_rationale: Leave balances change much more often than other employee attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the corporate hierarchy. History builds up as changes are captured.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position changes at its own rate and is used for reporting-line analysis.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_pay
satellites.description: Pay-rate history per employee: one row per effective rate-change date, with the hourly rate and the pay frequency.
satellites.split_rationale: Comes from its own source relation at a finer grain (employee + RateChangeDate), and the source keeps its history. EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity so this binding is valid.

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department group membership and last-change timestamp. History is captured over time to support as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift start and end times. Captured historically because shift definitions can be adjusted.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_details
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé (a structured document) and the last-modified timestamp.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. A missing EndDate marks the current assignment.

satellites.description: Descriptive product attributes.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive master data.

satellites.name: sat_product_pricing
satellites.description: Current standard cost and list price on the product record.
satellites.split_rationale: Financial figures change more often than descriptive data.

satellites.name: sat_product_lifecycle

satellites.description: Vendor identifying and descriptive attributes: vendor account number, company name and optional purchasing web service address.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing identity/description of the vendor, separated from the status codes that change more often.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_status
satellites.description: Vendor status codes with history: credit rating, preferred vendor status and active flag.
satellites.split_rationale: Status codes change at a different rate and need tracked history; carries the vendor ModifiedDate once.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_terms
satellites.description: Agreed standing supply terms per product and vendor: lead time, standard price and order quantity bounds.
satellites.split_rationale: Agreed contractual terms change rarely; split from operational running values.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_receipts
satellites.description: Running operational values on the supply relationship: last receipt cost and date, and quantity currently on order.
satellites.split_rationale: Running values change with every receipt/order, far faster than the agreed terms.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_details
satellites.description: Purchase order header state with history: revision number, status, order date and estimated shipment date.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle/status attributes tracked for status transitions and revisions.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_amounts
satellites.description: Purchase order monetary amounts: subtotal, tax, freight and total due.
satellites.split_rationale: Monetary amounts (different data type/concern) separated from lifecycle status.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_details
satellites.description: Ordered terms of a purchase order line: due date, ordered quantity, unit price and line total.
satellites.split_rationale: Order terms set at ordering, rarely changing; split from receipt progression.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_receipt
satellites.description: Cumulative receipt and inspection outcomes per line: received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities, with history of progression.
satellites.split_rationale: Receipt quantities change repeatedly over the order life; separate rate of change from ordered terms.

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_details
satellites.description: Shipping method rate terms with history: minimum charge (ship base) and charge per pound (ship rate). rowguid excluded as it has no business meaning.

evidence: Customer.AccountNumber is 'Unique number identifying the customer assigned by the accounting system'. No existing hub models customers.
It is an alternate identifier for the customer, not for any existing hub's key.
Customer.CustomerID is the table's own primary key. The vault has no customer hub.
Customer links to Person via PersonID and to Store via StoreID. It has its own surrogate key, which is not BusinessEntityID.
SalesOrderHeader.SalesOrderNumber is a computed unique order number. The vault has only purchase order hubs (PurchaseOrderID), which are a different concept (vendor-side).
SalesOrderHeader.SalesOrderID is the primary key of customer sales orders. hub_purchase_order is keyed by PurchaseOrderID and covers vendor purchasing, so no existing hub matches.
SalesOrderDetail is a composite-key line item of a sales order. hub_purchase_order_line belongs to purchase orders, a different business concept.
Store.BusinessEntityID is the same identifier as hub_business_entity's business key BusinessEntityID. The hub is already fed by Person, Employee and Vendor, which share this key space.
The Store column comment says 'Foreign key to Customer.BusinessEntityID'. That is imprecise, because Customer has no such column. The key name and format still match.
SalesPerson.BusinessEntityID comment: 'Foreign key to Employee.BusinessEntityID'. Employee already feeds hub_business_entity, so this is an explicit cross-reference to the same key.
SalesTerritory.TerritoryID is the primary key of a territory lookup. No existing hub models territories.
sat_state_province_territory is a satellite on state/province, not a territory hub.
SalesTerritory.Name is the description of a sales territory. Existing hubs keyed on Name (department, location and so on) are unrelated concepts. A shared column name is not evidence.
CreditCard.CreditCardID is the primary key for credit card records. No credit card hub exists in the vault.
CreditCard.CardNumber is an attribute or alternate key of credit card. No existing construct models credit cards.
Currency.CurrencyCode is the ISO currency code. The vault has no currency hub. hub_country_region is keyed on CountryRegionCode, which is a different code.
CurrencyRate is an exchange rate between two currencies on a date. The vault has no equivalent construct.
CurrencyRate.CurrencyRateID is the primary key of exchange rate records. The vault has no equivalent.
SpecialOffer.SpecialOfferID is the primary key of discount offers. The vault has no promotion or offer hub.
SpecialOffer.Description is the discount description. No existing hub models special offers.
SalesReason.SalesReasonID is the primary key of a purchase reason lookup. The vault has no such hub. hub_scrap_reason is a manufacturing concept.
SalesReason.Name describes a customer purchase reason. hub_scrap_reason, also keyed on Name, is a different concept.
ShoppingCartItem holds online cart contents. The vault has no cart or cart item construct.
ShoppingCartItem.ShoppingCartID is a cart identifier (nvarchar(50)). The vault has no shopping cart hub.
SalesTaxRate.SalesTaxRateID is the primary key of tax rates. The vault has no tax rate construct.
Customer.PersonID comment: 'Foreign key to Person.BusinessEntityID'. Person already feeds hub_business_entity, whose key is BusinessEntityID.
The CountryRegionCode column comment says 'Foreign key to CountryRegion.CountryRegionCode', which is the hub's business key. This is the same ISO code, in SalesTerritory and CountryRegionCurrency.

requirements.text: The warehouse must provide a consolidated, historical view of sales activity for reporting, performance management and planning.

References to products, people and business entities, employees, addresses, shipping methods and geography (countries/regions and states/provinces), which are maintained outside the sales area, must be preserved so that sales information can later be joined to those areas.
The business must be able to identify every customer by the customer account number assigned by the accounting system.
The customer account number uniquely identifies a customer.
The business must be able to distinguish an individual-person customer from a store customer.
For an individual customer, the business must retain the reference to the person who is the customer.
For a store customer, the business must retain the reference to the store.
The business must know the sales territory in which each customer is located.
The business must know when a customer's record was last changed in the operating system, so that reporting can be reconciled against the source.
The business must be able to report the customer base by territory.
The business must be able to report the customer base by customer kind (individual vs. store).
The business must be able to identify each store by its business entity reference.
The business must record the store name of each store.
The business must know which sales representative is assigned to each store.
The business must retain the store demographics captured for each store, covering the number of employees, annual sales and store type.
The business must be able to segment reseller performance by store demographic characteristics such as store size or store type.
The business must identify every sales order by its sales order number.
The sales order number is a unique sales order identification number.
The business must know which customer placed each order.
The business must know whether an order was placed online by the customer or entered by a sales representative, since this distinguishes the two sales channels.
For orders that were not placed online, the business must know which sales representative created the order.
The business must know the territory in which each sale was made, as recorded on the order itself.
The order's sales territory is held separately from the customer's territory and the representative's current territory, and reporting must be explicit about which territory is meant.
The business must track the date each order was created.
The business must track the date each order is due to the customer.
The business must track the date each order was shipped.
The business must track the current status of an order.
Order status must be one of the operational status values: in process, approved, backordered, rejected, shipped, cancelled.
The business must be able to measure order fulfilment performance, i.e. whether orders shipped on or before their due date.
The business must retain the customer's own purchase order number where the customer supplied one, so that reseller enquiries can be answered in the customer's own terms.
The business must retain the financial accounting number reference carried on the order, to allow reconciliation with finance.
The business must know the billing address used for each order.
The business must know the shipping address used for each order, as information separate from the billing address.
The business must know the shipping method chosen for each order.
The business must retain sales representative comments recorded against an order, as context for enquiries and disputes.
The business must be able to report order counts and values by channel, by territory, by representative, by customer and by period.
The business must track the revision number of an order, an incremental number tracking changes to the order over time.
The business must be able to tell that an order has been amended, and how many times.
The business must record the order subtotal.
The business must record the tax amount charged on the order.
The business must record the freight (shipping cost) charged on the order.
The business must record the total due from the customer for the order.
The order subtotal is the sum of the line totals for the order.
The total due from the customer is the subtotal plus tax plus freight.
The business must be able to analyse revenue with tax and freight separated from product revenue.
The business must know which credit card was used to pay for an order, where a card was used.
The business must retain the credit card approval code provided by the card company, for payment reconciliation and dispute handling.
The business must be able to report the share of orders paid by card versus those with no card recorded.
requirements.obj: share of orders paid by card

requirements.text: The business must know which currency exchange rate was applied to each order where the order was not in the company's base currency.
requirements.obj: currency exchange rate applied to order

requirements.text: The business must be able to report sales both in the transaction currency and converted to a reporting currency, using the rate that applied to the order.
requirements.obj: sales in transaction and reporting currency

requirements.text: The business must identify each order line within its order, using one incremental unique number per product sold.
The business must know which product was sold on each order line.
The business must know the quantity ordered per product on each order line.
The business must know the unit selling price of the product on each order line.
The business must know the discount amount applied to each order line.
The business must know the line total of each order line.
The line total is calculated as unit price × (1 − discount) × quantity.
The business must know which special offer (promotional code) applied to each order line, so that promotional effectiveness can be measured.
The business must retain the shipment tracking number supplied by the shipper for each order line, because lines of one order may ship separately.
The business must be able to analyse sales by product, by quantity, by realised price and by discount level.
requirements.obj: sales by product, quantity, price and discount

requirements.text: The business must be able to distinguish list-price revenue from discount given away at order line level.
The business must maintain the catalogue of sales reasons, each with a description and a reason category.
The business must know which sales reasons were recorded against each order.
An order may have several sales reasons, and a sales reason may apply to many orders.
The business must be able to report order volume and value by sales reason and by reason category.
requirements.obj: order volume and value by sales reason

requirements.text: The business must be able to report the proportion of orders for which no sales reason was recorded, as a data-quality measure.
requirements.obj: proportion of orders without sales reason

requirements.text: The business must identify each sales representative by their business entity reference, which is also their employee reference.
The business must know the territory a representative is currently assigned to.
The business must know each representative's projected yearly sales quota.
The business must know the bonus due to a representative if the quota is met.
The business must know the commission percentage a representative receives per sale.
The business must know each representative's year-to-date sales total and previous-year sales total as maintained by the operational system.
The business must be able to compare a representative's actual sales against quota and identify who is on track to earn the bonus.
The business must be able to report sales by representative over time, independently of the running totals held in the operational system.
The business must maintain the catalogue of sales territories, each with a territory name.
The business must know the country or region each territory belongs to.
The business must know the geographic group a territory belongs to, so that results can be rolled up regionally.
The business must know each territory's year-to-date sales and previous-year sales.
The business must know each territory's year-to-date business costs and previous-year costs.
The business must be able to report territory contribution, i.e. sales against costs, for the current and previous year.
The business must be able to roll territory results up to geographic group and to country/region.
The business must maintain the register of credit cards used for payment, identified by the card record held in the operational system.
The business must know the card type (card name), the card number, and the expiry month and year of each credit card.
The business must be able to report sales by card type.
Credit card numbers and expiry data are sensitive personal and payment information, and access to them must be restricted.
The business must state whether the card number is needed at all in the warehouse or whether a masked or partial value is sufficient.
The business must know which credit cards belong to which person.
A person may hold several credit cards, and a card may be associated with more than one person.
The business must be able to identify cards used on orders that are not registered to the ordering customer, as an input to fraud and data-quality review.
requirements.obj: cards used on orders not registered to the ordering customer

requirements.text: The business must retain shopping cart items, each identified within its shopping cart.
The business must know the shopping cart identifier for each cart item.
requirements.obj: shopping cart identifier of cart item

requirements.text: The business must know the product for each cart item.
The business must know the quantity ordered for each cart item.
The business must know the date and time each cart item was created.
requirements.obj: creation date and time of cart item

requirements.text: The business must be able to report which products are added to carts, and in what quantities.
requirements.obj: products added to carts and quantities

requirements.text: The business must be able to measure cart activity over time, using the creation date of cart items.
The business must maintain the catalogue of special offers, each with a discount description.
The business must know each special offer's discount percentage.
The business must know each special offer's discount type category.
requirements.obj: discount type category of special offer

requirements.text: The business must know the group the discount applies to (for example Reseller or Customer) so that promotions can be reported per channel.
The business must know each special offer's minimum quantity threshold.
The business must know each special offer's maximum quantity threshold.
The business must know each special offer's start date, the beginning of the period during which it is valid.
The business must know each special offer's end date, the end of the period during which it is valid.
The business must be able to determine which special offers were valid at any given date, including expired offers, so that historical orders can be explained.
requirements.obj: special offers valid at a given date

requirements.text: The business must be able to report revenue and discount attributable to each special offer, and to each offer type and category.
requirements.obj: revenue and discount per special offer, offer type and category

requirements.text: The business must know which products each special offer applies to.
An offer may cover many products, and a product may be covered by several offers.
The business must be able to check that the offer recorded on an order line was applicable to the product on that line, as a data-quality and pricing-governance control.
requirements.obj: applicability of order line offer to product

requirements.text: The business must maintain the list of currencies, identified by their ISO currency code, with the currency name.
The business must be able to present currency names in reporting rather than raw codes.
The business must retain exchange rates as a time series, recording for each rate the date and time the rate was obtained, the currency converted from, and the currency converted to.
The business must retain the average exchange rate for the day.
requirements.obj: average exchange rate for the day

requirements.text: The business must retain the final (end-of-day) exchange rate, as it serves a different reporting purpose than the average rate.

The business must be able to reproduce the exchange rate that was actually applied to a given order, not merely today's rate, so that historical reporting is stable and does not change when rates move.
The business must be able to report the same sales figures in more than one currency.
The business must state which rate (average or end-of-day) is used for each report.
requirements.obj: exchange rate type used per report

requirements.text: The business must be able to identify orders where no exchange rate was recorded and understand how those are to be treated (presumed base currency).
The business must know which currencies are used in which countries/regions.
A country/region may be associated with more than one currency, and a currency with more than one country/region.
The business must be able to check that sales in a given country/region were transacted in a currency valid for that country/region.
requirements.obj: validity of sales currency for country/region

requirements.text: The business must maintain the register of sales tax rates, each with a tax rate description.
The business must know the state, province or country/region each tax rate applies to.
The business must know the tax type for each rate, using the operational meanings: applied to retail transactions, applied to wholesale transactions, or applied to all sales.
The business must know the tax rate amount.
The business must be able to report tax collected by jurisdiction and by tax type.
requirements.obj: tax collected by jurisdiction and tax type

requirements.text: The business must be able to compare the tax amount charged on an order with the tax rates applicable to the relevant jurisdiction, as a compliance check.
requirements.obj: order tax amount with applicable tax rates

requirements.text: A sales order is placed by exactly one customer, and a customer may place many orders over time.
A sales order is handled by at most one sales representative, orders placed online by the customer have no representative, and a representative handles many orders.
A sales order is made in one sales territory, and a territory carries many orders.
A sales order consists of one or more order lines, and each order line belongs to exactly one order.
An order line sells one product, and a product is sold on many order lines.
An order line may be sold under one special offer, and an offer is used on many order lines.
A sales order may cite several sales reasons, and a sales reason may be cited on many orders.
A sales order may be paid with one credit card, and a card may be used on many orders.
A credit card may be registered to one or more people, and a person may hold several cards.
A sales order may use one currency exchange rate, and a rate may apply to many orders.
requirements.obj: sales order and currency exchange rate

requirements.text: A customer is located in one sales territory, and a territory contains many customers.
A customer is either a person or a store.
A reseller store is served by one sales representative, and a representative serves many stores.
A sales representative is currently assigned to at most one territory.
A sales representative has worked a series of territories over time.
A sales territory belongs to one country/region and to one geographic group.
A special offer applies to one or more products, and a product may be covered by several offers.
A country/region may trade in several currencies, and a currency may be used in several countries/regions.
An exchange rate converts from one currency to another on a given day.
A sales tax rate applies to one state/province or country/region for a given tax type.
A shopping cart contains one or more cart items, each for one product.
There is no recorded link from a shopping cart to a customer or to an order.
A sales order carries a billing address and a shipping address, which may differ.
A sales order is shipped using one shipping method.
The business must retain the full history of sales quotas per sales representative, including the quota date and the quota amount in force from that date.
The business must be able to determine the quota that applied to a sales representative at any point in the past.
requirements.obj: historical sales quota of a representative

requirements.text: The business must be able to compare the quota that applied to a representative in a past period with the sales actually achieved in that period.
The business must be able to report how a representative's quota has moved over time.
requirements.obj: quota movement over time per representative

requirements.text: The business must be able to report how often a representative's quota was revised.
The representative record also carries a single current quota figure alongside the dated quota history, and the business must be aware of this duality.
Reporting must state whether it uses the current quota figure or the dated quota history.
The current quota figure and the dated quota history must be reconcilable with each other.
The business must retain the history of which representative worked which territory, including the date the representative started work in the territory and the date they left.
A representative's territory assignment is open-ended, with no end date recorded, while the representative is still working the territory.
The business must be able to identify the currently active territory assignment for each representative.
The business must be able to determine who was responsible for a territory on any given date, so that historical sales can be credited to the person who actually held the territory at the time.
requirements.obj: representative responsible for a territory on a date

requirements.text: The business must be able to see the sequence of representatives who have held a territory.
The business must be able to see how long each representative held a territory.

The representative record also carries the currently assigned territory alongside the dated assignment history, the same current-versus-historical duality as for the quota, and the business must be aware of this.
Where an order's territory differs from the representative's territory at the time of the order, the business must be able to see and explain that difference.
requirements.obj: difference between order territory and representative territory at order time

requirements.text: Exchange rates are a daily time series, and the business needs the rate as at the relevant date.
requirements.obj: exchange rate as at relevant date

requirements.text: Exchange rates must never be retrospectively overwritten in reporting.
Special offers have explicit start and end dates.
The business must be able to determine the special offers that were live at any date, including expired ones.
requirements.obj: special offers live at a given date

requirements.text: The business must be able to see how descriptive information changes over time where it matters commercially, in particular a customer's territory, a store's assigned representative, a store's demographics, a special offer's discount percentage, and a territory's group.
requirements.obj: changes in descriptive information over time

requirements.text: Every record in this area carries a last-modified date and time.
The business needs the last-modified date and time as the primary signal that something has changed.
requirements.obj: last-modified date and time as change signal

requirements.text: The business needs the last-modified date and time as the basis for reconciling warehouse content with the operational system.
For all other entities in this area, the operational system holds only the current state.
The business must accept that history for entities holding only current state can only be built from the point the warehouse starts capturing it.
The business must decide for which current-state-only entities building history is worth doing.

The business must be able to report sales value and volume by period, territory, geographic group, country/region, representative, customer, customer kind, product, channel, currency, special offer and sales reason.
The business must be able to compare actual sales against quota per representative and per period, including the bonus and commission implications.
The business must be able to report territory profitability using sales and cost figures at territory level.
The business must be able to measure discounting: total discount given, by offer, by product, by channel and by customer kind.
The business must be able to measure fulfilment through order-to-ship elapsed time.
The business must be able to measure fulfilment through on-time-against-due-date performance.
requirements.obj: on-time delivery performance against due date

requirements.text: The business must be able to measure fulfilment through the distribution of order statuses.
The business must be able to measure channel mix, comparing online orders with representative-entered orders in volume and value.
The business must be able to report tax and freight separately from product revenue.
requirements.obj: tax and freight separately from product revenue

requirements.text: The business must be able to report sales in a single reporting currency across all territories, using the rate that applied to each order.
requirements.obj: sales in a single reporting currency

requirements.text: The business must be able to analyse the reseller base by store demographics and by assigned representative.
The business must be able to analyse online cart activity by product and period, within the limits of the missing link between shopping cart and customer or order.

The business must be able to see, for each order, whether the key commercial attributes are present: customer, territory, representative (where not online), currency rate (where non-base currency), and payment reference.
requirements.obj: presence of key commercial attributes on orders

requirements.text: The business must be able to check that the order total agrees with the sum of its lines plus tax and freight, and to report where it does not.
requirements.obj: order total against sum of lines plus tax and freight

requirements.text: The business must be able to check that line totals agree with quantity, unit price and discount as described by the source.
requirements.obj: line totals against quantity, unit price and discount

requirements.text: The business must be able to report orders that reference a special offer outside its validity period at the order date.
requirements.obj: orders referencing a special offer outside its validity period

requirements.text: The business must be able to report customers that are neither a person nor a store, or that are both, once the question of whether a customer is always exactly one of person or store is resolved.
requirements.obj: customers that are neither or both person and store

requirements.text: The business must be able to report representatives with no territory on any given date.
The business must be able to report territories with no representative on any given date.

The business must be able to reconcile operationally maintained running totals (representative and territory year-to-date and last-year figures) against totals recalculated from orders, and to report material differences.
requirements.obj: operational running totals against recalculated order totals

requirements.text: Each entity in this area must have a named business owner who is accountable for its definitions and for resolving the clarifications in the document.
Business owners for the entities in this area must be assigned before the warehouse is built.
Credit card data (card number, expiry, card type, holder association) is payment-sensitive.
Handling, retention and access rules for credit card data must be defined before it is loaded.
requirements.obj: handling, retention and access rules for credit card data

requirements.text: Individual customers are natural persons.
Personal-data handling rules, including retention limits and the treatment of deletion requests, must be defined for the customer information in this area.
requirements.obj: personal-data handling rules for customer information

requirements.text: Sales representative quota, bonus, commission and achievement figures are remuneration data about identifiable individuals and must be access-restricted to those with a legitimate need.
Store demographics are commercially sensitive information about reseller partners and must be treated as confidential.
Replication identifiers on several records have no business meaning and are not required by the business, but may be retained as a technical trace of the source record.
Values computed by the operational system (order number, customer account number, line total, order subtotal and total due) are to be taken as given from the source rather than recalculated.
Values computed by the operational system must be checkable by the business.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-003 says every customer is identified by the account number assigned by the accounting system, and REQ-004 says it uniquely identifies a customer. It is business-recognised and unique. REQ-057-3 says the source computes it and it is taken as given.

CustomerID is a system-generated surrogate in the source. The requirements do not name it as the identifier (REQ-003 prefers the account number), so it is a weak business key and works only as a fallback.

REQ-017 requires every sales order to be identified by its sales order number, and REQ-018 says it is a unique identification number. It is business-recognised, unique and mandatory. REQ-057-3 says it is taken as given from the source.
SalesOrderID is a system-generated surrogate. The requirements identify orders by order number (REQ-017), so it is a weak business key.

REQ-051 says an order line is identified within its order by one incremental unique number per product sold. The key is therefore the parent order reference plus the line number (REQ-042-2: each line belongs to exactly one order).
REQ-012 says each store is identified by its business entity reference. It is stable and recognised by the business.
REQ-067 says each sales representative is identified by their business entity reference, which is also their employee reference. It is stable, unique and mandatory.

The requirements (REQ-075, REQ-022, REQ-041-2) refer to territories as a catalogue with a name but give no explicit identifier. TerritoryID is the source reference, so it is a plausible but unconfirmed key.
REQ-075 says each territory has a territory name. It is business-recognised but not stated to be unique or stable.

REQ-082 says the register of credit cards is identified by the card record held in the operational system, which is CreditCardID. It is a system identifier but the requirements name it as the identification.

REQ-083 says the card number is known. It is sensitive (REQ-085, REQ-050-3), may not be needed in the warehouse (REQ-086), and is not stated to be unique or stable (cards expire and are reissued). It is a poor business key.
REQ-021-2 says currencies are identified by their ISO currency code. It is stable, unique, business-recognised and mandatory.

REQ-023-2 and REQ-057-2 describe a rate by the date and time obtained, the currency converted from and the currency converted to. This composite is the natural identification of a rate in the time series.
CurrencyRateID is a system-generated surrogate. The requirements do not name it as the identifier, so it is a weak business key.
REQ-008-2 and REQ-058 refer to special offers (promotional codes) without naming an identifier. SpecialOfferID is the source reference, so it is a plausible key.
REQ-008-2 says each offer has a discount description. It is not stated to be unique or stable, so it is a weak key.
REQ-062 says the sales reason catalogue has a description and a reason category but gives no identifier. SalesReasonID is the source reference, so it is a tentative key.
REQ-062 says each reason has a description (Name). It is business-recognised but not stated to be unique.
REQ-001-2 and REQ-002-2 say cart items are identified within their shopping cart and that the cart identifier is known for each item. The key is the cart identifier plus the item identifier.
REQ-002-2 and REQ-059-2 say a cart contains one or more items and each item carries the shopping cart identifier. It identifies the cart, but the requirements do not call it unique.

REQ-033-2 and REQ-058-2 describe tax rates by jurisdiction and tax type, with no explicit identifier. SalesTaxRateID is the source reference. The natural composite (state/province or country/region plus tax type) is an alternative.

REQ-006 says individual customers retain a reference to the person, and REQ-087 links persons to cards. The reference is maintained outside the sales area (REQ-002), so it is only an external reference and not a fully defined key.
REQ-002 and REQ-076 refer to countries/regions maintained outside the sales area. CountryRegionCode links territories and currencies (REQ-030-2), so it works as a reference key.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of a state or province, tracked over time; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Territory assignment changes independently and needs its own history.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_contact_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the contact relationship.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_details
satellites.description: Employee job and employment-status attributes: job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active/inactive flag, network login, and the last-modified timestamp.
satellites.split_rationale: Employment attributes that are not sensitive and change slowly. ModifiedDate is kept only here. rowguid is left out because it has no business meaning (REQ-006).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_sensitive
satellites.description: Restricted personal data about employees: national ID number, date of birth, gender and marital status.
satellites.split_rationale: Split out by data classification (PII), so access can be restricted to authorised HR users.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Leave balances (vacation and sick-leave hours remaining). The satellite builds a history of balance readings over time.
satellites.split_rationale: Leave balances change much more often than other employee attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the corporate hierarchy. History builds up as changes are captured.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position changes at its own rate and is used for reporting-line analysis.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_pay
satellites.description: Pay-rate history per employee: one row per effective rate-change date, with the hourly rate and the pay frequency.
satellites.split_rationale: Comes from its own source relation at a finer grain (employee + RateChangeDate), and the source keeps its history. EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity so this binding is valid.

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department group membership and last-change timestamp. History is captured over time to support as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift start and end times. Captured historically because shift definitions can be adjusted.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_details
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé (a structured document) and the last-modified timestamp.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. A missing EndDate marks the current assignment.

satellites.name: sat_product_details
satellites.description: Descriptive product attributes.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive master data.

satellites.name: sat_product_pricing
satellites.description: Current standard cost and list price on the product record.
satellites.split_rationale: Financial figures change more often than descriptive data.

satellites.name: sat_product_lifecycle
satellites.description: Sale availability and discontinuation dates.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle events change independently.

satellites.name: sat_product_cost_history
satellites.description: Standard cost history periods.

satellites.name: sat_product_list_price_history
satellites.description: List price history periods.

satellites.name: sat_product_category_details
satellites.description: Product category audit attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_subcategory_details
satellites.description: Product subcategory audit attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_details
satellites.description: Product model audit attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_catalogue
satellites.description: Structured catalogue content of the model.
satellites.split_rationale: Structured document content, separate data type.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_instructions
satellites.description: Structured manufacturing instructions of the model.
satellites.split_rationale: Structured document content, separate data type and audience.

satellites.name: sat_culture_details
satellites.description: Culture descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_product_description_details
satellites.description: Free-text marketing description.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Photograph file names.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_images
satellites.description: Binary photograph images.
satellites.split_rationale: Binary content split from simple fields.

satellites.name: sat_illustration_details
satellites.description: Illustration diagram.

satellites.name: sat_document_details
satellites.description: Document metadata, revision and approval control.

satellites.name: sat_document_content
satellites.description: Full binary document content.
satellites.split_rationale: Binary content, inclusion to be confirmed.

satellites.name: sat_unit_measure_details
satellites.description: Unit of measure name.

satellites.name: sat_location_details
satellites.description: Location hourly cost rate and capacity.

satellites.name: sat_scrap_reason_details
satellites.description: Scrap reason audit attributes.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_details
satellites.description: Work order quantities and dates.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_operation_details
satellites.description: Operation schedule, actuals, hours and costs.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_details
satellites.description: Live inventory transaction details.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source: live store.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_archive_details
satellites.description: Archived inventory transaction details.
satellites.split_rationale: Split by source: archive store.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_details
satellites.description: Review date, rating and comments.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_reviewer_pii
satellites.description: Reviewer identity (personal data).
satellites.split_rationale: PII classification split.

satellites.name: sat_product_location_inventory
satellites.description: Current quantity at shelf and bin.

satellites.name: sat_product_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Principal-image indicator.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of a component in an assembly.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_details
satellites.description: Component quantity per assembly and BOM level.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_details
satellites.description: Vendor identifying and descriptive attributes: vendor account number, company name and optional purchasing web service address.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing identity/description of the vendor, separated from the status codes that change more often.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_status
satellites.description: Vendor status codes with history: credit rating, preferred vendor status and active flag.
satellites.split_rationale: Status codes change at a different rate and need tracked history; carries the vendor ModifiedDate once.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_terms
satellites.description: Agreed standing supply terms per product and vendor: lead time, standard price and order quantity bounds.
satellites.split_rationale: Agreed contractual terms change rarely; split from operational running values.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_receipts
satellites.description: Running operational values on the supply relationship: last receipt cost and date, and quantity currently on order.
satellites.split_rationale: Running values change with every receipt/order, far faster than the agreed terms.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_details
satellites.description: Purchase order header state with history: revision number, status, order date and estimated shipment date.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle/status attributes tracked for status transitions and revisions.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_amounts
satellites.description: Purchase order monetary amounts: subtotal, tax, freight and total due.
satellites.split_rationale: Monetary amounts (different data type/concern) separated from lifecycle status.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_details
satellites.description: Ordered terms of a purchase order line: due date, ordered quantity, unit price and line total.
satellites.split_rationale: Order terms set at ordering, rarely changing; split from receipt progression.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_receipt
satellites.description: Cumulative receipt and inspection outcomes per line: received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities, with history of progression.
satellites.split_rationale: Receipt quantities change repeatedly over the order life; separate rate of change from ordered terms.

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_details
satellites.description: Shipping method rate terms with history: minimum charge (ship base) and charge per pound (ship rate). rowguid excluded as it has no business meaning.

satellites.name: sat_customer_details
satellites.description: Customer record change tracking and technical trace.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_store_details
satellites.description: Store name and change tracking.
satellites.split_rationale: Non-confidential store descriptors split from confidential demographics.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_store_demographics
satellites.description: Store demographics (employees, annual sales, store type); confidential.
satellites.split_rationale: Commercially confidential classification.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_sales_person_compensation
satellites.description: Representative current quota, bonus and commission; remuneration data, access-restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Remuneration terms change rarely; restricted classification.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_sales_person_performance
satellites.description: Representative running sales totals maintained by the operational system.
satellites.split_rationale: Running totals change frequently, unlike compensation terms.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_sales_quota_history
satellites.description: Dated sales quota history per representative.

satellites.name: sat_sales_person_territory_history_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of a representative's territory assignment; open-ended while current.

satellites.name: sat_sales_territory_details
satellites.description: Territory geographic group.

satellites.name: sat_sales_territory_financials
satellites.description: Territory running sales and cost totals.
satellites.split_rationale: Running totals change far more often than descriptive data.

satellites.name: sat_sales_order_details
satellites.description: Order dates, status, channel, references and comments.

satellites.name: sat_sales_order_amounts
satellites.description: Order financial amounts.
satellites.split_rationale: Financial measures grouped separately from descriptive order data.

satellites.name: sat_sales_order_payment
satellites.description: Credit card approval code; payment-sensitive.
satellites.split_rationale: Payment-sensitive classification.

satellites.name: sat_sales_order_line_details
satellites.description: Order line quantity, price, discount, line total and tracking number.

satellites.name: sat_sales_order_sales_reason_details
satellites.description: Change tracking for order sales reasons.

satellites.name: sat_sales_reason_details
satellites.description: Sales reason description and category.

satellites.name: sat_credit_card_details
satellites.description: Card type.

satellites.name: sat_credit_card_sensitive
satellites.description: Card expiry data; payment-sensitive, access-restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Sensitive payment classification.

satellites.name: sat_person_credit_card_details
satellites.description: Change tracking for person-card association.

satellites.name: sat_currency_details
satellites.description: Currency name.

satellites.name: sat_currency_rate_details
satellites.description: Average and end-of-day exchange rates.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_currency_details
satellites.description: Change tracking for country/region currency association.

satellites.name: sat_special_offer_details
satellites.description: Special offer description, discount terms and validity period.

satellites.name: sat_special_offer_product_details
satellites.description: Change tracking for offer-product coverage.

satellites.name: sat_sales_tax_rate_details
satellites.description: Tax rate description, type and amount.

satellites.name: sat_shopping_cart_item_details
satellites.description: Cart item quantity and creation time.

contracts.name: CountryRegionCurrency
contracts.doc: Mapping of country/region codes to the currency codes used in each, staged from the source CountryRegionCurrency table. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key integrity (CountryRegionCode, CurrencyCode); ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: CountryRegionCode
schema.description: Code identifying the country or region that uses the currency. Part of the business key.

schema.name: CurrencyCode
schema.description: Code identifying the currency used in the country or region. Part of the business key; corresponds to the currency code in the Currency asset.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: CreditCard
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset for credit card records from the Sales schema. Each record describes a payment card (type, number, expiry) identified by CreditCardID. This draft contract enforces the declared schema and business key; ownership and agreement are to be finalized at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint. Note: CardNumber is sensitive payment data and should be reviewed for masking/handling.

schema.name: CreditCardID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the credit card record (surrogate key in the source).

schema.name: CardType
schema.description: Type or brand of the credit card (e.g. the card issuer/network).

schema.name: CardNumber
schema.description: The credit card number. Sensitive payment data; handling and masking requirements to be confirmed by the reviewer.

schema.name: ExpMonth
schema.description: Month of card expiration.

schema.name: ExpYear
schema.description: Year of card expiration.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: Currency
contracts.doc: Reference list of currencies from the source Sales.Currency table, staged for the data vault. The contract enforces the declared schema, the CurrencyCode business key and not-null constraints; ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: CurrencyCode
schema.description: Code identifying the currency; business key of the asset.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the currency.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: CurrencyRate
contracts.doc: Currency exchange rates between a source and target currency for a given date, staged from the Sales.CurrencyRate source table. The contract enforces the declared schema, business key identity and not-null rules; value-level semantics are advisory unless noted.

schema.name: CurrencyRateID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the currency rate record (surrogate key in the source).

schema.name: CurrencyRateDate
schema.description: Date and time at which the currency exchange rate applies.

schema.name: FromCurrencyCode
schema.description: Currency code of the source currency being converted from; references Currency.CurrencyCode.

schema.name: ToCurrencyCode
schema.description: Currency code of the target currency being converted to; references Currency.CurrencyCode.

schema.name: AverageRate
schema.description: Average exchange rate for the day from the source currency to the target currency.

schema.name: EndOfDayRate
schema.description: Exchange rate at the close of the day from the source currency to the target currency.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: Customer
contracts.doc: Customer records from the sales source, staged one row per customer. A customer may be an individual (linked via PersonID) or a store (linked via StoreID) and may be assigned to a sales territory. The contract enforces the declared schema and business key; value-level constraints are not specified by the requirements, so none are asserted. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: CustomerID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the customer.

schema.name: PersonID
schema.description: Identifier of the individual person associated with the customer, if the customer is an individual.

schema.name: StoreID
schema.description: Identifier of the store associated with the customer, if the customer is a store.

schema.name: TerritoryID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales territory the customer belongs to.

schema.name: AccountNumber
schema.description: Account number assigned to the customer.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier (GUID) for the source record.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: PersonCreditCard
contracts.doc: Association between a person (identified by BusinessEntityID) and a credit card (CreditCardID) in the sales domain, staged from source table PersonCreditCard. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key integrity; ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (person) who holds the credit card. Part of the composite business key.

schema.name: CreditCardID
schema.description: Identifier of the credit card associated with the person. Part of the composite business key; references the CreditCard asset.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: SalesOrderDetail
contracts.doc: Line-item detail for a sales order: one row per product line on a SalesOrderHeader, including quantity, pricing, discount and computed line total. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key uniqueness/not-null (handled by the deterministic core). Ownership and agreement status are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: SalesOrderID
schema.description: Identifier of the parent sales order (references SalesOrderHeader).

schema.name: SalesOrderDetailID
schema.description: Unique identifier for the individual line item within the sales order.

schema.name: CarrierTrackingNumber
schema.description: Shipment tracking number assigned by the carrier for this line item; may be absent if not shipped.

schema.name: OrderQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product ordered on this line.

schema.name: ProductID
schema.description: Identifier of the product sold on this line (references Product).

schema.name: SpecialOfferID
schema.description: Identifier of the special offer applied to this line (references SpecialOffer).

schema.name: UnitPrice
schema.description: Selling price per unit of the product at time of order.

schema.name: UnitPriceDiscount
schema.description: Discount applied to the unit price for this line.

schema.name: LineTotal
schema.description: Line total for this item (derived from quantity, unit price and discount).

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier (GUID) for the record.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified.

contracts.name: SalesOrderHeader
contracts.doc: Sales order header records from the source Sales schema, with one row per sales order. It holds order-level dates, status, customer, territory, address, shipping, payment and currency references, and monetary totals. The contract enforces the declared schema and business key. No value-level semantic constraints are asserted, because no requirements state any. Ownership and agreement are left to human review.

schema.name: SalesOrderID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the sales order. It is the business key of the order header.

schema.name: RevisionNumber
schema.description: Revision number of the order. It tracks changes made to the order over time.

schema.name: OrderDate
schema.description: Date and time the sales order was created.

schema.name: DueDate
schema.description: Date the customer is due to receive the order.

schema.name: ShipDate
schema.description: Date the order was shipped to the customer.

schema.name: Status
schema.description: Current status code of the order. The allowed values are not stated in the requirements and need human review.

schema.name: OnlineOrderFlag
schema.description: Flag showing whether the order was placed online or through a sales person. The representation is not confirmed and needs human review.

schema.name: SalesOrderNumber
schema.description: Unique, human-readable sales order reference number.

schema.name: PurchaseOrderNumber
schema.description: Customer's purchase order reference number for the order.

schema.name: AccountNumber
schema.description: Financial accounting account number associated with the order.

schema.name: CustomerID
schema.description: Identifier of the customer who placed the order. It references Customer.

schema.name: SalesPersonID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales person who handled the order. It references SalesPerson.

schema.name: TerritoryID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales territory the order belongs to. It references SalesTerritory.

schema.name: BillToAddressID
schema.description: Identifier of the customer's billing address.

schema.name: ShipToAddressID
schema.description: Identifier of the customer's shipping address.

schema.name: ShipMethodID
schema.description: Identifier of the shipping method used for the order.

schema.name: CreditCardID
schema.description: Identifier of the credit card used for payment. It references CreditCard.

schema.name: CreditCardApprovalCode
schema.description: Approval code provided by the credit card company for the payment.

schema.name: CurrencyRateID
schema.description: Identifier of the currency rate applied to the order. It references CurrencyRate.

schema.name: SubTotal
schema.description: Order subtotal, before tax and freight, as a monetary amount.

schema.name: TaxAmt
schema.description: Tax amount charged on the order.

schema.name: Freight
schema.description: Shipping cost charged on the order.

schema.name: TotalDue
schema.description: Total amount due from the customer for the order.

schema.name: Comment
schema.description: Free-text sales representative comments about the order.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (ROWGUIDCOL) of the source row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason
contracts.doc: Association between sales order headers and the sales reasons recorded for them (many-to-many link). The contract enforces the presence and schema of the SalesOrderID and SalesReasonID keys and the ModifiedDate audit timestamp. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: SalesOrderID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales order (SalesOrderHeader) to which the sales reason applies.

schema.name: SalesReasonID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales reason (SalesReason) recorded for the sales order.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source system.

contracts.name: SalesPerson
contracts.doc: Sales representatives (salespeople) staged from the source SalesPerson table, with their assigned sales territory, quota, bonus, commission percentage and sales totals. The contract enforces the declared schema, business key and not-null rules; value-level semantics are not specified by requirements and are left for human review.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (employee) that is the salesperson; business key of the asset.

schema.name: TerritoryID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales territory currently assigned to the salesperson. May be absent if no territory is assigned.

schema.name: SalesQuota
schema.description: Projected yearly sales quota for the salesperson. May be absent if no quota is set.

schema.name: Bonus
schema.description: Bonus amount due to the salesperson.

schema.name: CommissionPct
schema.description: Commission percentage received per sale.

schema.name: SalesYTD
schema.description: Sales total for the salesperson year to date.

schema.name: SalesLastYear
schema.description: Sales total for the salesperson in the previous year.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier (GUID) used by the source system for replication.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: SalesPersonQuotaHistory
contracts.doc: Historical record of sales quotas assigned to sales people, one row per sales person and quota date. Sourced from the SalesPersonQuotaHistory source table. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key uniqueness/not-null; ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales person (business entity) to whom the quota applies.

schema.name: QuotaDate
schema.description: Date on which the sales quota became effective for the sales person.

schema.name: SalesQuota
schema.description: Sales quota amount assigned to the sales person as of the quota date.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Unique row identifier (GUID) for the record, as generated by the source system.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source system.

contracts.name: SalesReason
contracts.doc: Lookup of reasons a customer gave for purchasing a sales order (source: SalesReason). Contract enforces the declared schema, the business key SalesReasonID, and not-null on keys; value-level constraints are not specified by the requirements and are left for review.

schema.name: SalesReasonID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the sales reason; business key of the asset.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name or short label of the sales reason.

schema.name: ReasonType
schema.description: Category or type grouping the sales reason.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: SalesTaxRate
contracts.doc: Sales tax rates by state/province, staged from the source SalesTaxRate table. The contract enforces the declared schema and key fields; value-level semantics are advisory pending producer/consumer review.

schema.name: SalesTaxRateID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales tax rate record.

schema.name: StateProvinceID
schema.description: Identifier of the state or province to which the tax rate applies.

schema.name: TaxType
schema.description: Code indicating the category of tax the rate represents. Allowed values are not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: TaxRate
schema.description: Tax rate applied for the state or province.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name or description of the tax rate.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified.

contracts.name: SalesTerritory
contracts.doc: Sales territory reference data: one record per sales territory, with its name, country/region, sales group, and year-to-date and prior-year sales and cost figures. Source-to-staging contract; schema, primary-key and not-null breaches are enforced as hard by the core, and value-level semantics are alerting only pending human review.

schema.name: TerritoryID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the sales territory (business key).

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the sales territory.

schema.name: CountryRegionCode
schema.description: Code identifying the country or region the territory belongs to.

schema.name: Group
schema.description: Geographic grouping of the sales territory.

schema.name: SalesYTD
schema.description: Sales in the territory year to date.

schema.name: SalesLastYear
schema.description: Sales in the territory in the previous year.

schema.name: CostYTD
schema.description: Business costs in the territory year to date.

schema.name: CostLastYear
schema.description: Business costs in the territory in the previous year.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (ROWGUIDCOL) for the source row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: SalesTerritoryHistory
contracts.doc: Historical record of the sales territories assigned to each salesperson over time, with the start and end of each assignment. Staged from the source SalesTerritoryHistory table. The contract enforces the declared schema and the business-key identity of each record. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the salesperson (business entity) assigned to the territory.

schema.name: TerritoryID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales territory the salesperson was assigned to.

schema.name: StartDate
schema.description: Date and time when the salesperson's assignment to the territory began.

schema.name: EndDate
schema.description: Date and time when the assignment to the territory ended. Likely empty for a current assignment.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the source row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time when the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: ShoppingCartItem
contracts.doc: Items added to an online shopping cart prior to order placement, sourced from the Sales.ShoppingCartItem table. The contract enforces the declared schema, business key and not-null rules; no value-level constraints are stated in the requirements.

schema.name: ShoppingCartItemID
schema.description: Unique identifier for a shopping cart item row.

schema.name: ShoppingCartID
schema.description: Identifier of the shopping cart the item belongs to.

schema.name: Quantity
schema.description: Number of units of the product in the shopping cart.

schema.name: ProductID
schema.description: Identifier of the product added to the shopping cart.

schema.name: DateCreated
schema.description: Date and time the item was added to the shopping cart.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: SpecialOffer
contracts.doc: Sales promotions/discount offers (special offers) from the source SpecialOffer table, staged for the vault. Each record is identified by SpecialOfferID and describes the discount, offer type and category, validity window, and quantity bounds. Contract enforces the declared schema, primary key and not-null rules; value-level semantics are advisory pending producer/consumer review.

schema.name: SpecialOfferID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the special offer (business key).

schema.name: Description
schema.description: Text description of the discount or special offer.

schema.name: DiscountPct
schema.description: Discount percentage applied by the offer.

schema.name: Type
schema.description: Type of discount offered.

schema.name: Category
schema.description: Group or category the special offer belongs to.

schema.name: StartDate
schema.description: Date and time the special offer becomes valid.

schema.name: EndDate
schema.description: Date and time the special offer stops being valid.

schema.name: MinQty
schema.description: Minimum order quantity required to qualify for the discount.

schema.name: MaxQty
schema.description: Maximum order quantity to which the discount applies; may be absent when there is no upper bound.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Row-level globally unique identifier (GUID) assigned in the source system.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: SpecialOfferProduct

schema.name: SpecialOfferID
schema.description: Identifier of the special offer. References the SpecialOffer asset.

schema.name: ProductID
schema.description: Identifier of the product covered by the special offer.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier (GUID) for the record.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified.

contracts.name: Store

schema.name: rowguid

satellites. Review `review-queue.md` and `contracts/` before agreeing the model.
